prerequisites: Owned seeded lab auth2 (openlaw-docs-80ceef9e-auth2, Helix seed, light profile, random seed 7) built from 067c1646 with SMTP_URL and SMTP_FROM for Mailpit and BASE_URL http://127.0.0.1:43310; Daniel Okafor (Administrator) and Nadia Haddad (Legal Team Member) sign in with passwords; seeded and disposable Business Users (doc030-auth-*) sign in with links from the lab Mailpit.
Local OpenID Connect fixture (oauth2-mock-server 9.2.0) in container openlaw-docs-80ceef9e-auth2-oidc-1 as http://oidc:8080 on the lab network; the browser maps the name to the container address.
Owned unseeded lab auth2w (openlaw-docs-80ceef9e-auth2w) for first-run: the first Administrator DOC-030 admin-org Avery Morgan, created with the lab setup token.

Deployment phases applied by phase.sh with compose overlays: overlay-mail-stored.json (no SMTP_URL/SMTP_FROM), overlay-mail-incomplete.json (SMTP_URL without SMTP_FROM), overlay-mail-env.json (SMTP_URL and SMTP_FROM for 'DOC-030 Environment <env-relay@helix.example>'), overlay-baseurl-unset.json (no BASE_URL).
scenarios.expected: Administrators and Legal Team Members sign in with the methods enabled under Legal User Authentication. An Administrator with a password keeps emergency password sign-in when Email and password is off. Business Users sign in only with the methods enabled under Business Portal Authentication. Test mail reaches the controlled sink through the active configuration source. Invalid issuer/relay, denied domain, and locked environment settings have recoverable outcomes without exposing secrets.
scenarios.actual: 39 recorded browser steps passed as an Administrator. Settings → Advanced → Authentication showed Legal User Authentication and Business Portal Authentication, each with Email and password, Email magic link, Single sign-on (SSO) and Require two-factor authentication; SSO was disabled with the tooltip "Configure an identity provider below to enable single sign-on." Turning off the last method in either card showed "Enable at least one sign-in method." and stored nothing. With Legal Email and password off, Daniel still signed in with a password while Nadia got "Password sign-in is disabled for this account."; Nadia was refused on the Portal page too, and a Business User's password sign-in on the staff page landed in the Portal. With Business Email and password off, the Portal page offered no password choice, the staff page refused the Business User, and a sign-in link still worked. Pending staff invitations on helix.example and on the unlisted elsewhere.example got sign-in links ("It expires in 5 minutes and works once."), the first link sign-in turned each row Active, a spent link and a link opened after 316 seconds went to /auth/link-expired with no session. A Business User signing in on the staff page landed in /portal. Allowed email domains added northwind.example with a Remove control; a new northwind address became a Business User; an unlisted address got neutral pages, no mail and no account. After Remove northwind.example an existing Business User still got a new link, kept a held session, used an earlier link and a password; a new address got no link, was refused at password setup completion ("Password setup is no longer available for this address.") and at link redemption (EMAIL_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED); staff links still worked. The empty list read "No domains allowed yet. New users must be invited individually." and Invite user offered only staff roles. Turning off Business Email magic link made an earlier link fail with "This sign-in link could not be used. Request a new link or contact your administrator." Against the OIDC fixture: an unreachable issuer was refused ("The change could not be saved. Try again.") and stored nothing; registration turned on neither SSO switch; Legal SSO let an invited staff account sign in as Legal team member and turned its row Active; an uninvited helix.example identity got "Single sign-on failed. Try again." and no account; Save provider with a blank secret and with a rotated secret (tooltip "Leave blank to keep the current secret. Paste a new value to rotate.") each kept SSO working; an unreachable issuer update kept the previous issuer working; Business SSO admitted an existing Business User before and after its domain was removed and refused a new identity. With only SSO on for Legal users Daniel still signed in with a password, and turning Email and password back on and SSO off restored Nadia's password sign-in. Require two-factor authentication sent an Administrator without an authenticator to enrolment with "Your organization requires two-factor authentication.", each new session asked for a code, and magic-link, SSO and emergency password sign-ins were all sent to enrolment. In the first-run wizard, Skip optional steps opened Outbound email with no Set up later and Continue disabled; the relay form's Port followed Connection security (587/465/25) until edited; smtp:// and host:port were refused; a STARTTLS relay with Username and password saved without returning or storing the credentials in plain text and its test failed; Replace relay opened empty, Keep current relay closed it; Send test email showed "Test email sent to" the Administrator and "OpenLaw test email" arrived with Outbound email works, Sent through mailpit:1025 and From; an unreachable relay saved but failed its test; Clear relay stopped delivery and disabled Continue. Settings → Advanced → Outbound email showed Sender, Send test email and Replace relay (no Clear relay), Cancel kept the relay, and a replacement applied to the next email without a restart. With email unset the sign-in pages did not offer Email me a sign-in link. With BASE_URL removed, the Administrator saved Application address and saw "Settings saved. Restart the API and worker to apply changes."

scenarios.actual: 10 recorded steps passed for the operator responsibility: each is a deployment change on an owned lab (phase.sh recreates app and worker) followed by a browser check. With SMTP_URL and SMTP_FROM set while a stored relay was saved, the wizard read "Outbound email is set by the deployment environment. Mail is sent from DOC-030 Environment <env-relay@helix.example>." with no relay form and no Send test email, and a direct save answered 409; Settings → Advanced → Outbound email read "Managed by your deployment configuration. Contact your system administrator to change the relay." with only Send test email, and the test and a wizard invitation arrived from env-relay@helix.example, not the stored sender. With SMTP_URL but no SMTP_FROM, the wizard and Settings both showed "The deployment environment sets SMTP_URL but not SMTP_FROM, so mail cannot be sent. Set SMTP_FROM in the environment.", Settings disabled Send test email, and an invitation answered 409 with no mail. Removing the override and recreating app and worker made the stored relay active again (test mail from stored-relay@helix.example). The OIDC client was the local fixture; Register provider displayed "Paste this callback URL into your IdP console: http://127.0.0.1:43310/api/auth/sso/callback" on the BASE_URL address and GET /api/v1/auth/sso-providers did not return the secret. With BASE_URL set, Instance address showed "Application address Deployment configuration · Read only" and the callback used it. With BASE_URL removed, sign-in at the lab address failed with "Invalid origin" and the field became editable (Default, http://localhost:3000); after an Administrator saved http://127.0.0.1:43310 the callback still used http://localhost:3000 until app and worker restarted, then the field read Saved in OpenLaw, the callback used the saved address and sign-in at it worked again.

limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by a different agent from the author and the source reviewer; not a human user study and not feature-owner approval.
SAML: this version has no SAML setup; the Identity provider card offers OpenID Connect fields only. The scenario's SAML fixture check cannot run. The guide states it.

The identity provider was a local OIDC fixture (oauth2-mock-server 9.2.0), not a live provider; V-C37 requires a browser walkthrough, not a live-provider check. The existing openlaw-keycloak container was not used.

operator is a responsibility, not an OpenLaw account. Operator steps were compose overlay changes on the owned labs auth2 and auth2w, checked in the browser as the lab Administrator. The labs were destroyed after the walk.
With BASE_URL removed, the API accepts requests only from its default origin, so the Administrator reached the lab as http://localhost:3000 through a browser host mapping to the lab port.

Invalid issuer and invalid relay host refusals are recoverable but generic ('The change could not be saved. Try again.', 'One or more request fields are invalid.'). The guide gives the right corrective action without quoting them.

The author's open limitation is settled: a link whose method was turned off opens /portal/login with 'This sign-in link could not be used. Request a new link or contact your administrator.' and no session.
The per-address sign-in link limit ('Too many sign-in link requests. Try again later.') was observed on the shared work2 lab; the guide does not describe it.
The wizard's own Business-user portal step copy ('No domains allowed yet. Magic-link sign-in is unavailable.') was not checked; the author reports it as stale.

Two script helpers were made tolerant of a missing sign-in choice after the auth2w, policy, sso and twoFactor runs; in those runs the choices were present, so the recorded steps are unaffected (walkthrough.json scriptNotes).
